description.narrative:
In the arid regions of Somaliland, the Sool and Sanaag landscapes are home to thousands of displaced families and vulnerable host communities who have long depended on unsafe, saline water sources. Here, Oxfam is working to ensure lasting access to safe drinking water for 30,000 people across six localities through the construction of desalination plants, pipeline networks, and community tap stands.
The project goes beyond short-term relief by establishing locally led management systems, including trained water committees and cost-recovery mechanisms, to safeguard equity and sustainability. In a fragile context shaped by conflict and climate change, these efforts are laying the foundations for a model of sustainable water supply that can inspire solutions across the Horn of Africa and beyond.
Project Information: This project is providing sustainable access to safe and reliable drinking water for 30,000 displaced people and vulnerable host communities across six villages in the Sool and Sanaag regions of Somaliland. It is installing new desalination plants powered by renewable energy, building pipeline networks, and setting up community tap stands to replace unsafe and saline water sources. By using modern desalination technology, the project is transforming the way water is supplied in one of the driest regions in the world, where frequent droughts and degraded groundwater have left families at risk. It is also establishing locally led water management systems and cost-recovery mechanisms so thatcommunities can maintain the supply equitably and sustainably long after the project ends. In doing so, the project is not only responding to the urgent water crisis but also reducing protection risks, improving health outcomes, and creating a model for long-term water solutions that can be replicated across Somaliland and beyond.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
